chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Marry among the uncertain (in religion) but do not marry them (to your daughters), because the woman adopts the etiquette of her husband, and he compels her upon his religion.

key_terms.الشُّكَّاكِ: The uncertain ones (in religion), referring to the Nasibi

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying the Shukkaak and why should one avoid marrying daughters to them?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between marrying into the family of the *Shukkaak* (doubtful in faith, often the Nasibi) and marrying one's daughter to them, citing the sociological reality that a wife typically adopts her husband's religious identity. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving religious integrity within the household, as the husband's faith tends to dominate the domestic sphere, potentially leading to the wife's assimilation into his specific theological stance.
